intro: A harness is the durable layer around a model: procedures, constraints, memory, and human gates. The model is powerful; the harness is what makes it reliable.

layers.title: Skills
layers.subtitle: How to do a job
layers.body: Thin, named procedures the agent loads when a task matches — board bring-up, docs, PR hygiene, brand production. Detail lives on demand so every turn stays cheap.

layers.title: Rules
layers.subtitle: What must never go wrong
layers.body: Fail-closed constraints: secrets stay out of chat, outbound messages need clear approval, scripts must not overwrite source with redirects. Few always-on; most requestable.

layers.title: Memory
layers.subtitle: Curated, not a transcript dump
layers.body: Durable facts and decisions in a searchable store — people stances, project tickets, signed patterns — without pasting private inboxes into the public internet.

layers.title: Patterns
layers.subtitle: Kaizen with teeth
layers.body: Cross-cutting ways of working: propose → human sign-off → encode → apply → periodic review. The registry is the difference between lore and an operating system.

layers.title: Human gates
layers.subtitle: Irreversible stays human
layers.body: Desktop decisions for forks that matter. Speed is not an excuse to skip consent on send, publish, or destructive ops.

layers.title: Parallel lanes
layers.subtitle: Team-shaped solo work
layers.body: Named agent lanes with clear ownership and handoffs. Useful for product loops; dangerous without kyosei (co-prosperity) on shared benches.
